title: Why Government Bond Yields Are Rising and Causing Alarm
summary: Government borrowing costs have been surging around the world as investors demand more compensation to entice them to hold longer-maturity debt. Yields on 30-year Japanese government bonds are near all-time highs at 4.19%, while 30-year UK government bond yields are at their highest since 1998. A Bloomberg gauge tracking government debt across the Group of Seven countries now yields its highest on average since September 2000.

title: Stocks, Bonds Fall as Oil Jumps on US-Iran Jitters: Markets Wrap
summary: A surge in oil prices rippled through global markets, hitting stocks and bonds on worries that higher energy costs will fuel inflation and force the Federal Reserve to boost rates.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 1
summary: US oil prices topped $90 a barrel for the first time since late July as fresh American strikes on Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Dell, HP Enterprise Need Earnings to Validate Record Stock Runs
summary: Artificial intelligence fever is powering Dell Technologies Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. to their best years in the stock market.

title: US Strikes Targets in Iran Around Strait of Hormuz
summary: The US launched strikes against Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz, following Iran's attacks on commercial shipping and American forces in the region. Oil prices are spiking on the news. Tyler Kendall reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nasdaq 100 Drops as Traders Assess Oil Spike, Bond Jitters
summary: The Nasdaq 100 Index is retreating on Tuesday after coming off session lows, as investors weigh the effects of rising bond yields and higher oil prices on the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook.

title: Bond Slide Spreads to Emerging Markets on Fed Rate-Hike Bets
summary: A global bond selloff spread to emerging markets as investors dumped the riskier debt on expectations that the Federal Reserve will increase US interest rates later this month.

title: Global Bond Rout Sends Yields Soaring | Open Interest 9/1/2026
summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Global bonds tumble as yields surge to levels not seen since 2008, with soaring oil and renewed Middle East tensions fueling the selloff. Plus, a new era at Apple as John Ternus takes the reins. We’ll dig into Bobby Jain’s Millennium deal and the private-markets shakeout with Achilles Global Management CIO Sachin Khajuria. Plus, David Layton, the CEO of the Partners Group joins us to push back on concerns his move to CIO signals trouble. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fortress’s Burton Says Rates Still Poised to Go Higher
summary: Global bonds slumped as rising oil prices fueled inflation fears and bets on Fed rate hikes. Fortress Chief Strategist Elizabeth Burton says rates are still poised to go higher, arguing the underlying problem won’t be fixed without a fiscal response. She speaks on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Senegal Says Will Rework Debt as it Reaches New IMF Deal
summary: Senegal’s eurobonds fell on Tuesday after the government said it will move forward with a “debt treatment” under the Group of 20’s Common Framework and agreed a new $2.2 billion financing program with the International Monetary Fund.

title: Bond Market Selloff: Are Surging Yields a Threat to the Global Stock Rally?
summary: In equity markets, the myth goes that the only way is up. That perception has gained traction as global stock prices have largely ignored the selloff in bond markets. Yields on long-dated government debt have surged to near two-decade highs as investors worry about whether inflation and fiscal deficits can be tamed, and as sovereign bonds compete with an AI-fueled corporate borrowing boom.

title: Oil Extends Advance as US-Iran Escalation Revives Hormuz Risks
summary:
Oil rose for a second session as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, where crude carriers were hit by projectiles.
Leslie Palti-Guzman, Founder at Energy Vista, discusses the outlook for global energy as conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt flow. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Peru Inflation Just Tops Estimate to Hit Fastest Since 2023
summary: Inflation in Peru’s capital accelerated slightly more than expected in August, hitting the fastest pace in almost three years, pressured by housing and utilities including electricity and gas.

title: Italy’s League Faces Northern Split as National Future Surges
summary: A group of former members of Italy’s League has called for a revival of the party’s northern federal roots, openly challenging leader Matteo Salvini and adding to the pressure on him from the rise of the ultra-nationalist National Future party.

title: Uruguay acelera desdolarización con nuevos fondos Money Market
summary: Los inversores en Uruguay están colocando una mayor parte de su patrimonio en fondos Money Market y bonos del gobierno en pesos, lo que da un mayor impulso a los esfuerzos de este país sudamericano, considerado un refugio seguro, por reducir su dependencia del dólar.

title: Wells Fargo Analysts Join JPMorgan Traders in Turning Cautious on US Stocks
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. is the second bank to turn cautious on US stocks this week as the market heads into what is historically the worst month on the calendar for equities and upcoming midterm elections add to uncertainty surrounding the artificial-intelligence trade.

title: EU Considers Front-Loading Ukraine Loan as Funding Shortage Hits
summary: European Union member states are considering accelerating payments from the bloc’s €90 billion ($104 billion) loan to Ukraine as Kyiv faces a funding crunch, the bloc’s rotating presidency said.

title: US-Iran Tensions High After Strikes on Two Tankers in Hormuz
summary: US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz heightened after a flurry of military strikes at the start of the week, with neither side prepared to cede ground over the crucial waterway.

title: Partners Group CEO Rejects Redemption Concerns
summary: Partners Group CEO David Layton joined Bloomberg Open Interest to push back on concerns that his move to CIO signals trouble at the private-markets giant. He explains why the leadership shake-up isn’t tied to redemption pressure, says the firm is gaining fundraising share despite an industry slowdown, and reveals why elevated evergreen-fund redemptions could continue for another 12 to 18 months. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Redwire is Growing Strawberries in Space
summary: Redwire CEO Peter Cannito joins Bloomberg Open Interest to break down the next phase of the space economy—from orbital data centers and cheaper space manufacturing to the growing US, China space race. He also explains why falling transportation costs, SpaceX partnerships and even space agriculture could create major new commercial opportunities. (Source: Bloomberg)
